messages:
cameron: Heads up — planning a preemptive maintenance window for az3. Target window: Mon 2026-04-13 03:00-05:00 UTC. Scope: network switch firmware + rack fan firmware that both require rolling reboots. We'll do cohorted drains with warm backfill to avoid cold-cache latencies.

jess: Ack. Can you confirm which GPU pools are in the cohort sets and whether heavy embedding jobs get routed away?

cameron: Pools: gpool-az3-primary (latency), gpool-az3-batch (embeddings/batch), gpool-az3-reserve. Plan is 10% of nodes per cohort, 5m cordon/drain + 20m warm-backfill, then verify before next cohort. Embedding jobs will be steered to eu-west/az2 canaries for the duration.

tanya: Oncall note — I'll disable autoscaler scale-ups during the window to avoid churn and set SLO alert to 5xx/latency slack. Also will mute noisy infra-alerts but keep critical net/health alerts unmuted.

oliver: Recommendation: run prefix cache warmup for the latency pool after each cohort backfill. Warmup script idea below — sends short synthetic prefixes to prime KV cache and prefix caches: 

```bash
for p in $(seq 1 100); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \n    -d '{"model":"gpt-embedding-v1","input":"prefix warmup '$p'"}' >/dev/null
done
```

oliver: Run with concurrency 10 to avoid hitting rate limits.

ben: Quick cost Q — will backfill come from on-demand nodes or reserved? Need an estimate for the commit team.

cameron: On-demand for warm-backfill; expected delta ~ $1.1k-$1.5k for the window (ballpark). We can shift some traffic to dedicated reserved in eu-west to reduce peak if billing team wants to cap spend.

jess: We'll apply a 5% route override for embeddings to eu-west via the router policy: `route: region=eu-west weight=5%` for heavy batch jobs, leaving 95% on primary unless failures.

infra-bot: maintenance-scheduler: Created maintenance ticket MDF-2026-382 and scheduled for 2026-04-13T03:00:00Z. Incident channel: #inc-382.

tanya: Support ops — please publish a status page banner starting 02:50 UTC with expected impact: transient latency for embedding jobs and brief task evictions. Use the standard template and link to inc-382.

oliver: Networking ask: can net ops temporarily bump egress QoS for control-plane calls to avoid control path congestion during node reboots? If not, we may need to slow cohort cadence to 30m.

cameron: Good catch. @oliver I'll sync with netops now. If they can't bump QoS we'll push cohorts to 30m cadence. Current target cadence: cohort-1 03:00-03:25, cohort-2 03:35-04:00, cohort-3 04:10-04:35 (verification windows after each).

jess: Doing a dry-run in staging tomorrow 01:00 UTC with the same scripts + warmup. I'll post results in this thread.

cameron: Thanks all — please add any blockers. If netops gives go, we'll keep the 20m backfill cadence. :thumbsup:
